title.en: Work, energy and machines: hands-on activities from the textbook

text.en: Energy changes form as a pendulum swings, and a small effort can lift a heavy load with a lever. Chapter 7's activities show it.

Activity 7.1 drops a heavy ball into loose sand from 1 m and then 2 m. The higher drop makes a deeper depression because the ball has more energy.
Activity 7.2 uses a pendulum with a white sheet behind it. At the extreme positions it has only potential energy, and at the lowest point it has maximum kinetic energy.
Activity 7.3 pulls a cart up a plank with a spring balance and also lifts it vertically. The reading is smaller on the slope, so an inclined plane makes the effort smaller.
Activity 7.4 balances a stapler and an eraser on a scale over a pencil. This is a lever, and the position of the pivot decides how much effort is needed.
Activity 7.5 hangs a scale from its midpoint with a string as a beam balance and uses identical coins as weights.
Equal weights at equal distances from the fulcrum balance the beam.
A machine does not create energy. It lets a smaller force act over a longer distance or changes the direction of force.
Work is force times distance moved in the direction of the force.

problem.en: A force of 20 N moves a box 3 m in its own direction. How much work is done?

why.en: Unit of work is the joule.

prompt.en: How does a pendulum show the conversion of energy?

requiredIdeas.en: Potential energy highest at the ends
Kinetic energy highest at the lowest point

points.en: A higher drop gives more energy and a deeper dent.
A pendulum changes potential energy to kinetic energy and back.
An inclined plane reduces the effort needed.
A lever works on the pivot position.
